H6CA03158.name: Richard Pan
H6CA03158.bio: Physician, public health advocate and small business owner; former California state senator.

positions.stance: Will work to stop gutting of the Affordable Care Act, protect Medicare, stop insurers from denying doctor-prescribed care, and lower prescription drug costs.
Will hold President Trump and RFK Jr. accountable and fight for "facts and science" to guide federal policy on vaccination, public health, and the environment.
Will prioritize making necessities more affordable, loan relief for educational debt, and rolling back tariffs he says are raising prices.
Supports universal background checks, an assault weapons ban, and investment in first responders, mental health grants, and community-based violence prevention.
Will fight for a path to citizenship and believes ICE must be overhauled and replaced with an agency that enforces the law fairly and protects constitutional rights.

H6CA05195.name: Doris Matsui
H6CA05195.bio: U.S. Representative (Congresswoman) serving the Sacramento region for over two decades.

positions.stance: Opposes Trump's immigration tactics, votes no on funding ICE, and "opposes allowing masked ICE agents to disregard the rule of law."
Supports the Affordable Care Act and Medicare drug price caps, and cosponsored bills to repeal cuts to federal healthcare safety net funding.
Works to modernize and decarbonize the electric grid and support energy efficiency programs that save ratepayers money and cut emissions.
Supports stronger nationwide vehicle pollution standards and opposes attacks on California's vehicle emissions authority.
Supports protecting and restoring public lands and federal funding to plant city trees in low-income neighborhoods; opposes Park Service staff cuts.

H6CA07175.name: Mai Vang
H6CA07175.bio: Sacramento City Council member, teacher, and former Sacramento City Unified school board member and community organizer.

positions.stance: Refuses corporate PAC money: "you can't fight for working families while taking checks from the corporations making our lives harder."
Says tariff refunds belong to local businesses and families, and will fight to break up monopolies crushing neighborhood shops.
Will vote to "make billionaires pay their fair share and close corporate loopholes" to invest in communities.
Will raise the minimum wage tied to inflation, champion paid family leave and sick days, and push to pass the PRO Act.
Supports a moratorium on new data center construction, ending tax breaks for developers, and requiring them to cover the rate increases their energy use causes.

H0CA10149.name: John Garamendi
H0CA10149.bio: Rancher and U.S. Representative; former California Lieutenant Governor.

positions.stance: Supports "Make It In America" policies to bring manufacturing jobs back, stronger Buy America rules, and more infrastructure investment.
Supports Medicare negotiating drug prices, safe drug importation, rural hospital incentives, and "a national public option to increase competition."
Opposes education cuts and supports lower student loan interest rates, smaller class sizes, and federal investment in STEM education.
"America must take the climate crisis seriously"; advocates investment in clean energy, building weatherization, public transit, and biking amenities.
Opposes the Delta twin tunnels project: "Stop the tunnels, save the Delta."

H2CA00153.name: Rudy Recile
H2CA00153.bio: Small business owner, former U.S. Department of Agriculture employee, and retired U.S. Army Major with over 26 years of military service.

positions.stance: Says many veterans struggle to receive benefits due to bureaucratic processes and too few case workers.
Supports school choice, saying "School Boards are killing our education system" and curricula are not improving student proficiency.
Supports U.S. energy independence and criticizes shutting down power plants over opposition to carbon fuels.
"Government spending is out of control"; warns that printing money creates a pathway to hyperinflation.
Supports cutting prescription drug costs like insulin, repealing gas taxes in Washington and Sacramento, and getting housing costs under control.
Supports a $35 per month cap on insulin and bringing more doctors to the Valley so people can get care faster and closer to home.
Working to bring high-paying ag-tech, IT, and clean energy jobs to the Valley and supports trade deals that put local products and workers first.
Calls homelessness an emergency and supports investing in mental health and substance abuse services and job training.
Supports giving law enforcement "the tools they need to keep us safe," including federal funding to fight methamphetamine and fentanyl trafficking.

H4CA09101.name: John McBride
H4CA09101.bio: Strength and conditioning coach for over 40 years, including at the University of the Pacific and St. Mary's High School.

positions.stance: Priorities include removing dangerous chemicals from food and water, "Medical Freedom," natural healing methods, and "No Death Boards."
Supports local law enforcement, criminal prosecution, a stronger southern border, and mental health initiatives.
Supports water rights for an abundance of water and reducing government influence on small, private farms.
Supports reducing "Oppressive Tax Policies," drastically shrinking government spending, no tax on Social Security, and energy independence.
Priorities include education, youth and family support, mental health services, and homelessness.

H0CA10073.name: Mark DeSaulnier
H0CA10073.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 10th District; former California State Senator and member of the California Air Resources Board.

positions.stance: "Workers, not just tech companies, deserve a voice" as AI reshapes jobs; fighting to protect the right to organize and wages that keep up with costs.
Advancing transit-oriented housing and federal investments to bring down housing costs, and working on cleaner transportation that reduces commutes.
Fighting to protect California's vehicle emission standards and clean energy investments, and advocating Delta water protection and fossil fuel worker transition programs.
Says trust "is built by showing up and being accountable," citing more than 260 town halls.
Supports letting local newspapers operate as nonprofits and letting news organizations negotiate with tech platforms for fair compensation.

H6CA10187.name: Jeff Frese
H6CA10187.bio: Small business owner who built a national snack brand and has since run consumer companies.

positions.stance: Supports 8-year term limits, banning members of Congress from trading stocks, "No budget, no pay," and closing the lobbying revolving door.
Supports stopping deficit spending, cutting building red tape, and banning Wall Street and hedge funds from buying single-family homes.
"Back the police. Prosecute crime." Supports ending cashless bail and real consequences for fentanyl dealers.
Supports voter ID for federal elections, paper ballots, making Election Day a national holiday, and keeping vote by mail.
Supports no federal income tax on teachers, money to classrooms, back-to-basics instruction, shop class and trades, and "Parents in charge."

H6CA11268.name: Connie Chan
H6CA11268.bio: San Francisco Supervisor for District 1 and chair of the Board of Supervisors Budget Committee; former legislative aide.

positions.stance: Will fight for Medicare for All, restore ACA subsidies, and reverse Medicaid cuts.
Would cap childcare costs at no more than 7% of family income and guarantee universal pre-K for children ages 3-5.
Will strengthen Buy America policies and invest in manufacturing and construction to support union job creation.
Would unwind Trump-era tax cuts benefiting the wealthiest, enact a federal corporate minimum tax, and expand a fully refundable Child Tax Credit.
Would restore full funding and independence to the National Labor Relations Board.

H8CA11116.name: Scott Wiener
H8CA11116.bio: California State Senator; former San Francisco Supervisor and Deputy City Attorney.

positions.stance: "We need Medicare for All"; meanwhile supports capping insulin at $35/month, lowering drug prices, and reversing cuts to Medicaid and the ACA.
Supports allowing people to sue ICE when it violates their rights, and says he will "fight to protect our immigrant neighbors and ABOLISH ICE."
Calls for lowering housing costs and building 8 million new homes, citing his housing streamlining laws in California.
Will pass a comprehensive data privacy law and social media protections, and take California's net neutrality law national.
Believes decisions about pregnancy, abortion, and contraception belong to individuals and their doctors, "not politicians."

H4CA12154.name: Lateefah Simon
H4CA12154.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 12th District; former BART Board director and community organizer.

positions.stance: Will champion closing loopholes in federal gun laws, stopping illegal firearms, and funding mental health, addiction treatment, and recidivism prevention.
"Housing is a fundamental right"; will advocate ending landlord discrimination and increasing rental subsidies so residents can stay in their homes.
Will push to use federal funds to turn empty government buildings into emergency shelters and build more transitional housing.
Supports a living wage, labor law reforms ensuring collective bargaining, and a 12-week paid federal family and medical leave program.
Supports a public option and ultimately "an affordable single-payer health system," plus expanding Medicare drug price negotiation to all drugs.

H6CA12209.name: Jamie Joyce
H6CA12209.bio: Researcher working in AI, democracy technology, and charity.

positions.stance: Says she has never taken corporate PAC money or special interest money.
Supports AI guardrails, including red-line regulations and interim safeguards, and requiring an evidence-based federal plan for AI's impacts.
Wants accountability on the Epstein files, including records from agencies like the Treasury, IRS, and intelligence agencies.
Has drafted legislation to "Delete the surveillance state," "Get ICE off our streets," and "Shine a light on dark money."
Built a tool to collect issues voters publicly raise across the district to inform project appropriations.

H2CA13115.name: Adam Gray
H2CA13115.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 13th District and UC Merced instructor; former California State Assembly member.

positions.stance: Working to lower costs of food, housing, health care, and utilities; introduced a bill to reverse Medicaid cuts and extend ACA premium tax credits.
Works to ensure reliable water deliveries for farmers, weakening regulatory barriers while securing funding for new water storage infrastructure.
Works to ensure farmers, ranchers, and dairymen "have the resources, support, and certainty they need to continue feeding the country."
Believes learning, training, and job preparation from good schools "will propel students into the world."
"Strongly supports law enforcement" and is committed to policies cracking down on drugs and gang violence.

H4CA09093.name: Kevin Lincoln
H4CA09093.bio: Former Mayor of Stockton and U.S. Marine Corps veteran.

positions.stance: "National security starts with border security"; will fight to secure the border and enforce immigration laws.
Will work to cut wasteful government spending and lower taxes.
Will fight "soft-on-crime policies like early prisoner release and reduced sentences for repeat offenders."
Supports the President's AI Action Plan, saying it prioritizes American innovation, removes burdensome regulations, and builds domestic AI infrastructure.
Supports the CLARITY and GENIUS Acts, opposes IRS broker rules covering software developers, and supports the right to self-custody digital assets.

H6CA14163.name: Melissa Hernandez
H6CA14163.bio: BART Board Director and former Mayor of Dublin; former small business manager in the dental and health sectors.

positions.stance: Will work to drive down housing, healthcare, and childcare costs, protect Social Security and Medicare from cuts, and grow small businesses.
Will fight to give police, firefighters, and emergency responders training and resources, and invest in mental health crisis response and fentanyl treatment.
Will work to lower raw material costs, incentivize new housing, and help first-time homebuyers with down payments and home loans.
Supports expanding the Child Tax Credit, recruiting and paying childcare workers more, and Paid Family and Medical Leave.
Will prioritize lowering prescription drug costs, protecting and expanding Medicare, and restoring insurance subsidies; supports the Women's Health Protection Act.

H0CA15213.name: Aisha Wahab
H0CA15213.bio: California State Senator and Assistant Majority Leader; former Hayward City Council member.

positions.stance: Will ban junk fees nationwide, take on monopolies and price-gouging, and cut prescription costs.
Supports building housing at all income levels and stopping Wall Street and private equity from buying single-family homes.
Will lower premiums and drug prices and "move toward universal, affordable healthcare"; protect Medicare and Medi-Cal from cuts.
Will protect Title I and IDEA funding, protect Pell grants, expand apprenticeships, and add campus mental health supports.
Will ban congressional insider trading, defend voting and civil rights, and treat war "as a last resort."

H2CA14162.name: Kevin Mullin
H2CA14162.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 15th District since 2022; former local business owner who has served in local and state office.

positions.stance: Will "continue to fight back against authoritarianism in the courts, in our communities, and at the ballot box."
Supports getting dark money out of elections, expanding ballot access, and cosponsors the Freedom to Vote Act.
Opposes the Medicaid cuts in the 2025 budget bill and cuts to National Institutes of Health research funding.
Member of the YIMBY Caucus; introduced the Empty Lots to Housing Act to turn underused lots near transit into housing.
Cosponsors the Green New Deal and introduced the FARE Act to speed electrification of commuter rail.
"Believes in smaller government, stronger communities, secure borders, and a future where families can thrive."
"Supports American energy production to lower costs and reduce reliance on foreign nations."
"Our veterans deserve better healthcare, better support, and respect for their service."

H4CA16197.name: Sam Liccardo
H4CA16197.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 16th District, in his first term.

positions.stance: Leads bipartisan bills to speed construction of affordable and market-rate housing, and authored the RESIDE Act to convert vacant offices into housing.
Introduced the Fix It Act, a bipartisan ACA premium tax credit extension designed to lower premiums while saving taxpayer dollars.
Introduced the Keep Innovators in America Act to retain U.S.-educated international talent, and drafted legislation to prepare workers for AI-driven industries.
Established the Wildfire Resilience Partnership and works to reduce wildfire-related property insurance costs.
Authored the MEME Act to stop elected officials profiting from cryptocurrency schemes, and bills addressing unlawful military deployments in American cities.

H6CA16176.name: Peter Soulé
H6CA16176.bio: Former executive in his family's Soule Steel business and former San Jose Civil Service Commission member.

positions.stance: Would withhold federal dollars from cities with sanctuary policies and oppose local policies that limit Second Amendment rights.
Supports ending "waste, fraud and abuse," including defunding the California High-Speed Rail project.
Would "make energy more affordable by removing restrictions on drilling for oil and building refineries in California."
Supports banning large financial institutions from buying single-family homes and shielding home sellers like Baby Boomers from capital gains tax.
Supports parental rights, school choice, vocational training, and federal funding only for schools focused on basic skills and "fair and balanced" American history.

H0CA17193.name: Ritesh Tandon
H0CA17193.bio: Engineer and businessman with two decades in Silicon Valley technology.

positions.stance: Supports targeted middle-class relief, stronger market competition, and cracking down on hidden junk fees "without expanding bureaucracy."
Supports federal incentives for new housing supply, rewarding faster local permitting, and first-time homebuyer savings tools.
Supports making college and career pathways more affordable, expanding career and technical education, and increasing teacher pay in California.
Supports lowering out-of-pocket and prescription drug costs, healthcare price transparency, and expanded access to preventive and primary care.
Opposes "layered tax increases and commuter-punishing fee schemes"; supports simpler compliance and tax fairness for workers, retirees, and small businesses.

H4CA16049.name: Zoe Lofgren
H4CA16049.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 18th District; former immigration attorney and immigration law professor.

H6CA18172.name: Shane Lewis
H6CA18172.bio: U.S. Marine Corps veteran, church worship leader and elder, and small business owner teaching music.

positions.stance: Would tie Title I funds to schools showing proven core-subject instruction and at least 10% gains in student proficiency within one year.
Would tie a portion of education funding directly to students and reaffirm parents' right to guide their child's education.
Supports "an all-of-the-above energy strategy," including clean-tech investment, natural gas as a bridge, hydrogen, and hydroelectric power.
Supports expanding legal pathways and reforming the H-2A visa program with rigorous vetting, while prioritizing American workers.
Supports counting only U.S. citizens for apportioning House seats and reserving Census-based federal funding primarily for citizens.

H6CA20152.name: Jimmy Panetta
H6CA20152.bio: U.S. Representative first elected in 2016 and member of the Ways and Means Committee; former Alameda County prosecutor.

positions.stance: Working to lower prices with federal investment in roads, rail, research, manufacturing, broadband, and water, and supports expanding child care and equal pay.
Supports blocking oil drilling off the coastline and on public lands, cutting carbon emissions, and investing in wildfire prevention and clean energy.
Supports expanding federal tax credits to build low- and middle-income housing and support first-time homebuyers and renters.
Supports universal health care, lowering prescription drug prices for seniors, and protecting "a woman's right to choose her own reproductive healthcare."
Working to pass legislation to deter presidential abuses of power and insulate elections from illicit interference.

H6CA19154.name: Peter Coe Verbica
H6CA19154.bio: CFP Principal and Managing Director at Silicon Private Wealth, a money management firm.

positions.stance: Calls to "End the high taxes on gas and ill-conceived reformulated blends."
Supports lowering food costs "by Providing Water for Farmers."
Calls to "Fix the CA Insurance Crisis."
Supports providing "Neighborhood autonomy over housing."
Calls to "Stop PAGA's Assault on CA Businesses."

H4CA20181.name: Vince Fong
H4CA20181.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 20th District since 2024; former district director for Congressman Kevin McCarthy.

positions.stance: Supports unleashing "responsible domestic energy production to lower costs for families and small businesses."
Supports modernizing water storage and conveyance and stopping "policies that send water out to sea."
Supports ensuring the armed forces have the tools and technology they need, and investing in aerospace leadership.
"A secure border is fundamental to national sovereignty"; supports enforcing existing laws while supporting legal immigration.
Opposes restricting law-abiding gun owners' rights, favoring enforcement of existing laws and holding violent offenders accountable.

H6CA20228.name: Sandra Van Scotter
H6CA20228.bio: Direct Support Professional serving adults with developmental disabilities; former respiratory therapist.

positions.stance: Supports Medicare for All and amending the Constitution to make Medicare a right; would work to reverse H.R. 1's Medi-Cal cuts.
Says disability support systems are chronically underfunded and will bring her Regional Center experience to Congress.
Will hold town halls for veterans and military families and ensure veterans know what benefits they are entitled to.
Will fight for "sustainable, fair water policy that serves farmers, residents, and future generations."
Supports a pathway to legal status for undocumented workers, "similar to the amnesty passed under the Reagan administration."
Committed to growing the San Joaquin Valley's economy, including federal investment in food innovation and regional job programs.
Supports federal funding for law enforcement and first responders, helping domestic violence victims, and cracking down on fentanyl.
Believes "women, not politicians should be making their own healthcare decisions"; cosponsors the Women's Health Protection Act.
Working to reform "our broken healthcare system," citing the $35 insulin cap and $2,000 out-of-pocket limit on prescription drugs.
Supports "comprehensive, bipartisan immigration reform that keeps families together, secures our borders, and fixes our broken immigration system."
